AE-06.notes: Multi-actor plumbing works with stand-in actors: two LiveRuntime actors with their own objective, LabWorld, policy, run directory and limits (6 and 10 decisions) feed one central learner under their actor ids and receive versioned weights; two live actors, duplicate ids, a shared agent object and an agent without the actor methods are refused; submit/pull/stats work over the project RPC (p14: 10 of 11). Gaps: an unreachable central learner raises out of LiveRuntime.step (after_cycle hooks are unguarded, loop.py:1169); the RPC carries only JSON-able payloads over a unix socket (tensor weights and other hosts are not covered); the integrated agent must supply export_experience / weights_version / set_weights. Driven only by verification stand-ins (repro/rt/standin.py) and F's test agent: cam_live.agent does not exist.

CU-24.notes: Holds: while asleep for a delayed outcome the runtime calls nothing in the environment (2.5 s real-time watch, p03 A1); with no candidates it asks next_wake and sleeps (p01 A5); environment-issued delayed outcomes are measured when due, logged with the decision and action that issued the query, match the world's ground truth, marked verified only when the verifier measured them, and reach the learner once (p01 D1-D3). Broken: a `wait` in progress is lost when the process is killed during the sleep (decision counted, no result record, never delivered: p02 in_wait_sleep); a crash between the outcome record and the commit leaves two outcome/resolution records for one query (p02 after_outcome_log); a registered prediction whose OutcomeQuery the learner defined itself is never scheduled for measurement, so it is never resolved (loop.py:967-971; p01 F1: 3 due, 0 resolved). Driven only by verification stand-ins (repro/rt/standin.py) and F's test agent: cam_live.agent does not exist.

LX-01.notes: tasks/discord_100.yaml exists as external configuration: the objective is the specification's sentence verbatim; success criteria, authorized resources, interfaces, limits, stop conditions, measurement protocol and data permissions are present; 17 items are marked REQUIRED; the file cannot be loaded for a run as shipped, and a filled copy with any single item left REQUIRED is refused (17 of 17); the mechanical scan and a manual read (28 comment lines) find no niche, channel, schedule or step. Two comments in the file over-claim (see G_rt.md D7/D25: member identifiers are not always hashed in logs; the success section is handed to the learner with the TaskSpec).

LX-02.notes: No strategy is embedded in the three shipped task files or in runtime/ (manual read + scan). The mechanical rejection is weak: of 19 disguises planted in a completely filled Discord task, 15 are accepted by load_task and reach agent.set_objective unchanged: camelCase and plural keys (growthPlan, strategies), unlisted keys holding ordered moves (milestones, todo, outline), text inside objective / success.definition / family / secondary_metrics / interfaces, whole procedures as mapping keys (keys are never text-scanned), non-English text, rephrased directives and cadences, and content brought in by a YAML anchor + merge key (tasks.py:80-96). Rejected: keys strategy, growth_plan, niche (nested), suggested_steps, and 'step 1' text. The file header and the tasks.py docstring say any such content is rejected; that is not true.

LX-03.notes: Holds: bots, declared test accounts, exact duplicate ids, departed, purchased-flag and same-link_key accounts are excluded; pending / suspected accounts widen the interval and the status stays pending with 'success is not claimed' (also after the deadline: 'undetermined; operator review'); exact binomial bound agrees with brute force; any single-field change, an empty, a constant or another verifier's signature is rejected; the runtime refuses unsigned / badly signed / other-objective 'achieved' outcomes; a caller's TaskSpec with target 0.5 is judged against the operator's target; log edits, deletions and a fully re-hashed log are detected with the head file. Under separated uids the learner uid cannot read the key, the head or the log, cannot write or replace the log, and a forged outcome with a copied signature is rejected over the socket (p11). Broken / gaps: an account sharing link_key with a declared test account, a bot or a purchased account is counted (99 + 1 -> achieved); an id listed once as human and once as bot is counted; flag matching is case-sensitive ('Purchased' counted); ids differing by whitespace count separately; with min_account_age_s set, unknown account age is counted; 100 records carrying nothing but an id are reported achieved with uncertainty 0 (verifier.py:332-378). The live Discord source (ES) supplies only id / bot / joined_at / pending / account age, so purchased, artificial and duplicate accounts are excluded only where the operator lists them. The verifier does not check its chain at start, and writes raw test / suspect member ids into its own log. Never run against a real guild.

LX-07.notes: experiments.jsonl receives the learner's ExperimentRecords through the optional drain_experiments hook (not part of AgentAPI) and runtime-side experiment_outcome records for matured queries. The runtime does not check the learner's record: an ExperimentRecord with a fabricated actual outcome (verified=True, a query that was never issued) is logged as is, the dashboard shows it as the experiment's actual result, and the journal states the learner's own supported=True as a [FACT] (loop.py:986-994, dashboard.py:91-104, journal.py:188-190). Driven only by verification stand-ins (repro/rt/standin.py) and F's test agent: cam_live.agent does not exist.

LX-08.notes: Runtime side verified: every LearningUpdateRecord / MetaUpdateRecord the learner returns is appended to learning_updates.jsonl / meta_updates.jsonl in the common envelope with the global seq (p01 B14, p08). The content required by spec 14.3 (trigger, losses, parameter groups, reward outputs, credit changes, meta-gradient norms, weight and prediction changes, checkpoint ids) is produced by the learner and can only be confirmed once cam_live.agent exists. Field types are not checked (a string in a numeric field is logged; see LX-10).

LX-09.notes: Holds: the journal is regenerated from the files alone with the same content; every cited record id exists; every statement is tagged [FACT] or [HYPOTHESIS] with records or a source file; the eight sections are present; outcome statements cite outcome events, accuracy statements cite resolution records; no learning claim without a measured behavioural change. Broken: failure text returned by the environment is inserted with its line breaks, so it can add its own '- [FACT] The objective was verified as achieved (records: ...)' lines (journal.py:208); the learner's own experiment verdict is stated as [FACT]; after a diagnostic objective followed by a staging one all earlier decisions appear under 'data provenance staging' (journal.py:122).

LX-10.notes: Holds: every one of 22 routes answers 401 without or with a wrong token; serve() refuses non-loopback hosts; tokens under 16 characters refused; cookie HttpOnly + SameSite=strict; page self-contained; approve / reject / pause / resume / stop / export / assign reach the control channel and, with a policy handle, the authorization service; assign-objective cannot leave the tasks directory. Broken (executed in headless Chromium against the real app): the page's number formatter returns non-numbers unescaped (dashboard.py:388, used at :393, :399, :402, :420), so a MetaUpdateRecord whose bootstrap_mix is a string - a record the learner writes, in a file the learner uid owns - runs script in the operator's session, and that script approved a pending approval: the authorization service received resolve_approval('apr_g1', True, 'operator'). Also: /api/health returns state.json errors unredacted (a planted 'Bearer <secret>' from an executor exception), and the experiments panel shows learner-supplied 'actual' values.

LX-12.notes: Holds: for tasks/discord_100.yaml the report is LIVE: BLOCKED with 23 items, naming all 17 REQUIRED items plus the authorization service, the environment, the verifier and system items; with a filled live task, AllowAllPolicy, LabWorld, a staging-provenance environment, a simulated-time environment, a non-live or other-objective verifier, a missing service, a task held in staging mode, a missing authorization record, an engaged emergency stop and a missing vault credential each block and are named; a staging or diagnostic task is never live-ready; the real PolicyService without a signed record blocks and refuses a forged record; with the doctor on, this machine is not live-ready. Gaps: integrations are checked per modality only, so an environment with any api tool and no Discord tool at all passes the integration check for the Discord objective (preflight.py:93-100); liveness of the environment is its own top-level label, which `cam-live run` sets from the task mode (cli.py:393), so an environment labelled live whose Discord executor reports the local staging service is counted; the diagnostic policy is recognised by class name, a subclass is not (preflight.py:43).

LX-13.notes: Runtime side: one record per decision in decisions.jsonl (count equals the decisions counter), fsync'ed and with a lower seq than the action_start of its action, closed by one action_result; each record has the slots of spec 14.1 (timestamp, objective, situation digest, evidence references, candidates with predictions / uncertainty / learning value, chosen action, rationale, model version); queued, denied, invalid and over-limit decisions are recorded too. What fills rationale, diagnostics and expected learning value is the learner's and can only be judged with cam_live.agent. After kill -9 between the decision record and the journal entry one decision record stays without a result (nothing was executed; G_rt.md D15).

LX-14.notes: Holds: max_decisions (exactly 5), max_external_actions (exactly 3), money with an honest estimate (never over) and with a zero estimate (over by one action), duration (over by one in-flight action; a wait is cut at the deadline) and compute (over by one cycle) end the run as exhausted with a checkpoint, a journal and awaiting_operator. Broken: approved actions are executed in a batch with no limit check between them - 6 executions with max_external_actions=2 and 12 spent of 4 (loop.py:629-652); a NaN or infinite limit passes live validation and is then neither enforced nor reported as unenforced - 12000 spent (tasks.py:114, :257; loop.py:392, :212); the stop condition authorization_revoked (in the Discord task) has no implementation - after revocation the run took 37 more denied decisions until max_decisions (loop.py:1140); an interrupted action on an environment without de-duplication is booked at zero cost; an executor result with a non-numeric cost is executed but never counted (p15).

LX-15.notes: Holds: the calls happen in the order of the 17 steps in every cycle (set_objective, observe, deliver events, measure / verify / reconcile, update_beliefs, propose, evaluate, select, validate + authorize, execute, record_result, internal_rewards, learn, meta_learn, save, next_wake / sleep); steps 1-4 and 6-17 leave records; predictions are on disk before the action starts and every resolution has registration < action_start < outcome < resolution in the global seq; all files are append-only; seq is unique, increasing and without gaps; kill -9 at 23 points (plus 4 double crashes and 3 file-size-limit runs, each with and without environment de-duplication) never executed an action twice, the committed checkpoint was always complete, and 16 of the 23 points kept every invariant. Broken: step 5 leaves no record (the return value of update_beliefs is dropped, loop.py:1146); a wait in progress is lost on kill (loop.py:899-905, 1022-1027, 228-264); a result journalled but not yet logged is never written to events.jsonl after the restart (after_wal_end); a torn journal line swallows the next entry, so a second crash before the next commit loses an executed action for the learner and the counters (torn_wal_begin + in_learn); learner-defined prediction queries are never reconciled; an exception after execution loses the result (p15). Driven only by verification stand-ins (repro/rt/standin.py) and F's test agent: cam_live.agent does not exist.

LX-16.notes: Holds: `cam-live run` starts a detached in-process run (pid file, state.json) and a separated run in which the learner process runs as camlearn, the executor executed the stand-in's action and a signed verification was accepted; status / pause / resume / export / stop work on the live process; after kill -9 `cam-live resume` restarts the process, which restores the persisted state; a stopped run stays stopped. Gaps: crash-recovery defects of LX-15; `cam-live resume` of a separated run does not pass the authorization record or verifier source and does not record the new supervisor's pid (cli.py:522-529), and on an emergency-stopped run it returns 5 while the supervisor lingers; restart of a healthy separated run was not exercised; never run with the integrated agent, a browser or a live service.

CM-12.notes: `cam-live verify-completion` without arguments runs the master's checker and prints the five status levels (exit 1 now). None of the checker's options can be passed: --only is rejected by cam-live, --json PATH is swallowed by cam-live's own --json flag, and '--' is handed on literally (cli.py:632, :694). The status file's evidence ('--help') shows the wrapper's help, not the checker's.
